title: The Resurrection and Ascension
overview: Luke 24 presents the climactic conclusion of the Gospel, detailing the resurrection of Jesus Christ, His post-resurrection appearances, and His ascension into heaven. The chapter begins with the discovery of the empty tomb by the women, followed by Jesus’ revelation to two disciples on the road to Emmaus. It culminates with Jesus appearing to the gathered disciples, affirming His bodily resurrection, opening their understanding of Scripture, and commissioning them to preach repentance and forgiveness. The chapter closes with Jesus’ ascension and the disciples’ joyful worship. This chapter is foundational for Christian faith, confirming Jesus as the risen Lord and empowering His followers for mission.
structure:
**Verses 1-12: The Empty Tomb and Initial Reports.** The chapter opens with the women visiting Jesus’ tomb, finding it empty, and encountering angelic messengers who remind them of Jesus’ prophecy about His resurrection. Despite their testimony, the apostles initially doubt until Peter investigates.

**Verses 13-35: The Road to Emmaus.** Two disciples journey to Emmaus, discussing recent events when Jesus joins them unrecognized. He explains Scripture concerning Himself, and their eyes are opened during a shared meal, leading to renewed faith and immediate witness.

**Verses 36-49: Jesus Appears to the Disciples.** Jesus appears to the assembled disciples, dispelling their fears by showing His physical wounds and eating before them. He teaches them that His suffering and resurrection fulfilled Scripture, commissions them to preach repentance and forgiveness, and promises the coming of the Holy Spirit.

**Verses 50-53: The Ascension and Worship.** Jesus blesses His disciples and ascends to heaven. The disciples respond with worship and continual praise in the temple, marking the beginning of the church’s mission empowered by joy and the Spirit.

keyVerses.text: He is not here, but is risen: remember how he spake unto you when he was yet in Galilee,
keyVerses.significance: This verse proclaims the central truth of the resurrection, affirming Jesus’ victory over death and fulfilling His own predictions. It anchors the chapter’s message of hope and divine power.

keyVerses.text: And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.
keyVerses.significance: Jesus’ explanation of Scripture reveals the unity of the Old Testament testimony about the Messiah, underscoring the divine plan and fulfillment in Christ’s life, death, and resurrection.

keyVerses.text: Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have.
keyVerses.significance: This verse affirms the bodily resurrection of Jesus, countering any notion that He was a mere spirit. It confirms the physical reality of His risen state, essential for Christian doctrine.

keyVerses.text: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
keyVerses.significance: This commissioning verse establishes the global mission of the church, linking repentance and forgiveness to the risen Christ and marking the start of the gospel’s worldwide proclamation.

keyVerses.text: And it came to pass, while he blessed them, he was parted from them, and carried up into heaven.
keyVerses.significance: The ascension marks the exaltation of Christ and His enthronement at God’s right hand, signifying the completion of His earthly ministry and the inauguration of His heavenly reign.

characters.name: Jesus Christ
characters.description: The risen Lord who appears multiple times in this chapter, revealing Himself bodily, explaining Scripture, commissioning His disciples, and ascending to heaven. He is the central figure whose resurrection validates His messianic identity and mission.

characters.name: The Women at the Tomb
characters.description: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and others who first discover the empty tomb and receive the angelic message. They serve as the initial witnesses to the resurrection, tasked with proclaiming this truth despite initial disbelief from others.

characters.name: The Two Disciples on the Road to Emmaus
characters.description: Followers of Jesus who are initially confused and disheartened by His death. Their encounter with the risen Christ and the opening of Scripture transforms their understanding and faith, prompting immediate witness.

characters.name: The Eleven Disciples
characters.description: The core group of Jesus’ followers who receive the resurrection news, experience Jesus’ post-resurrection appearances, and receive the Great Commission. Their transformation from doubt to boldness is pivotal for the early church.

characters.name: The Angels
characters.description: Heavenly messengers who appear at the tomb to announce Jesus’ resurrection and remind the women of His prior predictions, affirming divine authority and fulfillment of prophecy.

themes.description: The chapter centers on Jesus’ resurrection as the cornerstone of Christian faith, demonstrating His victory over death and confirming His divine identity. This theme connects to the broader biblical narrative of redemption and eternal life.

Jesus’ explanation of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms shows that His life, death, and resurrection were foretold and necessary. This theme emphasizes the unity and divine inspiration of Scripture.

The initial skepticism of the disciples contrasts with their eventual belief after encountering the risen Christ. This theme highlights the journey from doubt to faith, encouraging perseverance in belief.
Jesus commissions His followers to preach repentance and forgiveness to all nations, establishing the church’s mission. This theme underscores the responsibility of believers to proclaim the gospel.
Jesus’ ascension signifies His return to divine glory and the completion of His earthly work, preparing the way for the Holy Spirit’s coming and the church’s empowerment.

historicalContext: Luke 24 is set in first-century Judea shortly after the crucifixion of Jesus, during the early morning of the first day of the week, which corresponds to Sunday. The cultural context includes Jewish burial customs such as anointing the body with spices and sealing the tomb with a large stone. Politically, Judea was under Roman occupation, with Jewish religious leaders holding limited authority. The resurrection narrative would have been countercultural, confronting prevailing Jewish expectations of the Messiah and Roman skepticism about claims of resurrection. The use of Old Testament scriptures reflects the Jewish milieu and the early Christian effort to interpret Jesus’ life and mission within that framework.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology emphasizes the sovereignty of God in the resurrection, viewing it as the definitive proof of Christ’s victory over sin and death. The chapter’s focus on Scripture fulfillment underscores the authority of God’s Word and the necessity of faith in Christ alone for salvation.

Dispensationalists highlight the literal bodily resurrection and the future hope it guarantees. They often stress the distinct roles of Israel and the church, seeing the commission in verse 47 as the beginning of the church age with a worldwide gospel mission.

Early church fathers like Augustine and Chrysostom interpreted Luke 24 as affirming the historicity of the resurrection and the continuity of God’s redemptive plan. They emphasized the transformative power of Christ’s appearances and the importance of the ascension for Christ’s heavenly priesthood.

crossReferences.connection: Paul affirms the resurrection of Christ as the gospel’s core, paralleling Luke 24’s emphasis on the risen body and fulfillment of Scripture.
Acts records the ascension of Jesus, complementing Luke 24’s account and emphasizing His exaltation and promise to return.
John’s resurrection appearances to the disciples provide additional detail on Jesus’ bodily resurrection and the disciples’ initial doubts and faith.
This Old Testament prophecy about God not abandoning His Holy One to decay is cited in Luke 24 as fulfilled in Jesus’ resurrection.
The suffering servant prophecy explained by Jesus on the road to Emmaus is foundational for understanding His atoning death and resurrection.
The Great Commission parallels Luke 24’s mandate to preach repentance and forgiveness, highlighting the church’s mission.

application: Trust in the reality of Christ’s resurrection as the foundation of your faith and hope.
Seek to understand Scripture deeply, allowing Christ to open your heart to its true meaning.
Embrace the mission to share the gospel of repentance and forgiveness with boldness.
Overcome doubt by encountering Jesus through prayer, fellowship, and the Word.
Celebrate and worship God continually, recognizing His power and presence in your life.
Depend on the Holy Spirit’s empowerment as promised by Jesus for effective Christian living.
conclusion: Luke 24 powerfully affirms the resurrection of Jesus as the cornerstone of Christian faith, revealing Him as the fulfillment of Scripture and the risen Lord who commissions His followers to proclaim repentance and forgiveness. The chapter’s vivid accounts of Jesus’ appearances, teaching, and ascension provide assurance of His victory over death and His ongoing presence through the Spirit. For believers today, this chapter encourages steadfast faith, diligent study of Scripture, joyful worship, and faithful witness empowered by God’s Spirit, anchoring the church’s mission in the risen Christ.
timeline: c. AD 30-33 - Resurrection and Ascension of Jesus Christ

The forgiveness or pardon of sins, a key aspect of the gospel message preached by the apostles.
To wait or remain; used here to describe the disciples’ instruction to wait in Jerusalem for the Holy Spirit.
An ancient measure of distance equal to about one-eighth of a mile, used to describe the distance to Emmaus.
A reference to the Holy Spirit, whom Jesus promised would empower the disciples after His ascension.

outline.heading: The Empty Tomb and Angelic Announcement
outline.description: Women discover Jesus’ tomb empty and receive a message from angels confirming His resurrection, though initial disbelief persists among the disciples.

outline.heading: The Road to Emmaus Encounter
outline.description: Two disciples meet the risen Jesus without recognizing Him; He explains Scripture concerning Himself, and their faith is awakened when He breaks bread with them.

outline.heading: Jesus Appears to the Disciples
outline.description: Jesus appears to His disciples, proving His physical resurrection, teaching the fulfillment of Scripture, commissioning them to preach, and promising the Holy Spirit.

outline.heading: The Ascension and Worship
outline.description: Jesus blesses His disciples and ascends to heaven, prompting their joyful worship and continual praise in the temple, marking the beginning of their empowered ministry.
